answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because whisper only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, meadow is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any marble approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
